title: Natural Gas Pipeline & Compressor Station Ordinance Extraction Schema
description:
Regulatory requirements for natural gas pipelines, compressor stations, and associated infrastructure.

SCOPE: Natural gas compressor stations, natural gas pipelines (transmission, distribution, gathering), metering/regulator stations, and associated pipeline infrastructure.

EXCLUDE: 
  - Oil and gas wells (conventional or unconventional), geothermal wells, wind turbines, solar installations, water/sewer utilities, electric substations, telecommunications towers
  - Dimensional standards that apply ONLY to residential/commercial uses with no natural gas facility linkage (multi-family restrictions, duplex rules, retreat lot rules). NOTE: lot size, front/side/rear yard, and zoning-district rules ARE in scope when the ordinance applies them to a gas facility — see GAS-APPLICABILITY TEST.
  - Non-gas-specific land uses (duplex residence, commercial space, office buildings)

EXTRACTION DISCIPLINE: When extracting from multi-use ordinances, ONLY extract provisions that explicitly apply to natural gas compressor stations, natural gas pipelines, or metering/regulator stations. If a provision regulates 'structures' generally without mention of gas pipeline infrastructure, EXCLUDE it. If noise/distance rules apply to gas compressors specifically, INCLUDE them. Use applies_to field to mark the facility type.

SITING-CRITICAL FOCUS: Extract ONLY requirements that directly determine site viability for a natural gas pipeline or compressor station developer. Ask: "Does this value tell a developer whether this site is physically possible or legally compliant?"

EXTRACT:
  - Setback distances: all numeric values (feet/meters from property lines, roads, water bodies, sensitive uses)
  - Noise LIMITS: only the actual dBA/dB ceiling values (e.g., 55 dBA max, 65 dBA daytime). These determine site viability.
  - Fencing: numeric height requirements AND qualitative presence/opacity mandates that constrain buildability (e.g., "a solid opaque fence shall enclose the compressor yard", "security fencing required around all equipment")
  - Enclosure: whether an enclosure is required or prohibited, quantitative OR qualitative (e.g., "all compressor units shall be housed in a fully enclosed building", "open-air compressors prohibited"). Use value_category='qualitative' with the mandate in requirement_description when no numeric magnitude is stated.
  - Minimum lot size: minimum acreage or square footage required to site the facility
  - Zoning districts: districts where the facility is permitted by right, allowed by conditional/special use, or prohibited
  - Yard setbacks (front, side, rear) and generic structure setbacks when applied to a gas facility

DO NOT EXTRACT (operational, not siting-critical):
  - Noise monitoring protocols, testing durations, deadlines, submission requirements, ambient measurement procedures, complaint-response timelines, noise mitigation equipment standards (acoustic blankets, mufflers, barriers)
  - Fencing material composition, locking/gate hardware specs, landscaping and buffer-tree planting schedules. KEEP fencing height and any required/prohibited fencing mandate.
  - Enclosure architectural finish details (accent materials, column spacing, decorative elements, roof pitch). KEEP the underlying required/prohibited enclosure mandate.
  - Any rule_kind=monitoring, rule_kind=deadline, rule_kind=duration, rule_kind=submission FOR the noise feature UNLESS there is an associated quantitative limit value

SEMANTIC CLARITY (distance features):
  - 'property lines distance': setback from jurisdiction boundaries or neighboring property edges
  - 'distance between compressor stations': separation between gas compressor facilities
  - 'roads distance': setback from street/right-of-way centerline or edge
  - 'water bodies distance': setback from rivers, streams, wetlands
  - 'schools/hospitals/community structures distance': setback from sensitive land uses
  - 'structures distance': generic building/structure setback, ONLY when no occupancy type is named. Prefer a named-type feature whenever the ordinance names one. EXCLUDE definition clauses that describe what occupies a setback zone rather than stating a numeric distance (e.g., 'structures, equipment or appurtenances shall not occupy any required setback' — this defines the setback area, not a setback distance from structures).
  - 'front yard distance': street-facing lot line setback for the facility.
  - 'minimum lot size': minimum parcel area for the facility (acres or sq ft).
  - 'zoning districts': districts permitting/prohibiting the facility (qualitative, applicable_values holds district codes).

AMBIENT REFERENCE PATTERNS (noise):
  - For limits like 'shall not exceed [ambient baseline] + X dB', capture as: value=X (the adder), value_category='quantitative', value_interpretation='above_ambient'; include the baseline description (e.g., '72-hour evaluation baseline') in notes if not already in source_verbatim
  - Example: 'ambient + 7 dB daytime' → value=7, units='dB', specific_subject='daytime adder', value_interpretation='above_ambient', notes='pre-development ambient level or 72-hour evaluation'

Every requirement row is decomposed on four axes: WHAT is regulated (feature + specific_subject + requirement_description + applies_to), HOW MUCH (value + value_category + value_interpretation + units + ambient_reference_level + range_low/range_high), HOW BINDING (obligation), and WHEN/WHERE (condition + applies_to). Evidence lives in source_verbatim, summary, reasoning, and section.

document_applicability.description: Scope verification (extraction-quality field, excluded from compiled output). Use this to confirm the document actually regulates natural gas pipelines or compressor stations, not just general zoning or other utilities.

applies_to_natural_gas.description: Does this document contain provisions regulating natural gas pipelines, compressor stations, or metering/regulator stations? Set to FALSE if the document only contains general zoning rules (residential, commercial, industrial) that do not explicitly mention natural gas compressor/pipeline infrastructure.

extraction_approach.description: Which sections were extracted vs excluded. Format: 'Extracted [sections]; Excluded [sections]'. MUST include explicit statement about what was REJECTED. Example: 'Extracted Sec 5.2 (compressor stations), Sec 6.1 (noise), Sec 4.3 use table (districts permitting gas facilities), Sec 5.4 (compressor lot area and yards); Excluded Sec 3 (residential-only dimensional table, retreat lot rules, duplex restrictions)'

jurisdiction.description: Geographic and temporal context. These fields become row-level context in compiled output.

state.description: US state name or abbreviation exactly as written in document.

county.description: The specific municipality (city, town, township, borough, or village) that enacted this ordinance. CRITICAL: Use the QUERIED_JURISDICTION value from the CONTEXT block if present — it is the authoritative name. Do NOT use the county or regional name even if it appears prominently in the document. If 'Bristol County' or 'Allegheny County' appears in the document but QUERIED_JURISDICTION says 'Rehoboth' or 'Oakmont', use that. Strip only the administrative suffix: 'Town of Rehoboth' → 'Rehoboth', 'City of Weatherford' → 'Weatherford'. Capture the administrative category in jurisdiction_type instead.

subdivision.description: Sub-jurisdiction name if applicable. Null if county-level.

jurisdiction_type.description: Type of jurisdiction: County, City, Town, Township, Borough, or Village.

year.description: Year the ordinance was adopted or last amended. Null if not stated.

source.description: URL or document reference for the source ordinance. Use the SOURCE_URL from the CONTEXT block at the top of the document if present.

requirements.description:
Regulatory requirements extracted from the ordinance.

SCOPE VALIDATION (Critical for all extractions):
  - EXTRACT ONLY: Rules that explicitly govern natural gas compressor stations, pipelines, or metering/regulator stations
  - EXCLUDE: Oil and gas well rules (conventional or unconventional well drilling, production, or wellpad requirements)
  - EXCLUDE: Dimensional rules that apply solely to residential/commercial uses with no gas linkage (multi-family restrictions, duplex rules, retreat lots)
  - INCLUDE: Lot size, front/side/rear yard, and zoning-district rules WHEN applied to a natural gas facility, whether stated directly or via a use table naming gas/utility/energy uses
  - EXCLUDE: Land use restrictions that do not name or clearly reference gas facilities
  - Test: If the rule applies equally to office buildings, residential, and industrial without gas mention, EXCLUDE it
  - Use applies_to field to confirm gas facility type (e.g., 'Compressor station', 'Natural gas pipeline')

SITING-CRITICAL FOCUS: Extract ONLY requirements that directly determine site viability for a natural gas pipeline or compressor station developer. Ask: "Does this value tell a developer whether this site is physically possible or legally compliant?"

EXTRACT:
  - Setback distances: all numeric values (feet/meters from property lines, roads, water bodies, sensitive uses)
  - Noise LIMITS: only the actual dBA/dB ceiling values (e.g., 55 dBA max, 65 dBA daytime). These determine site viability.
  - Fencing HEIGHT: only numeric height requirements (minimum/maximum feet or inches)
  - Enclosure requirements: only if hard required/prohibited with a measurable parameter

DO NOT EXTRACT (operational, not siting-critical):
  - Noise monitoring protocols, testing durations, deadlines, submission requirements, ambient measurement procedures, complaint-response timelines, noise mitigation equipment standards (acoustic blankets, mufflers, barriers)
  - Fencing material specifications, locking mechanism requirements, gate lock specs, screening/landscaping/buffer trees
  - Enclosure architectural details (accent materials, column spacing, decorative elements)
  - Any rule_kind=monitoring, rule_kind=deadline, rule_kind=duration, rule_kind=submission FOR the noise feature UNLESS there is an associated quantitative limit value

DISTANCE FEATURE SPECIFICITY:
  - Use 'structures distance' ONLY when the ordinance declines to name an occupancy type ("any occupied structure", "all buildings"). If a type is named, use the specific feature. Never emit both for one clause.
  - Use 'front yard distance' for street-facing lot line setbacks; use 'property lines distance' with specific_subject='rear yard'/'side yard' for the other two faces.
  - Use 'property lines distance' ONLY for setbacks from property boundaries (not general zoning)
  - Use 'roads distance' for street/right-of-way setbacks
  - Use 'distance between compressor stations' for gas-to-gas separation
  - Use 'water bodies distance', 'schools distance', 'hospitals distance' for sensitive land uses ONLY if linked to gas facility (e.g., compressor setback from school)
  - When multiple distance targets appear in one regulation (e.g., 'from property line AND from road'), create separate rows with distinct feature values

EXTRACTION RULES:

(1) ONE ROW PER REQUIREMENT: Each distinct regulatory provision gets its own row. When a single regulation applies to multiple subjects (e.g., 'compressor setback from property lines and from road centerline'), create SEPARATE rows with different 'specific_subject' values.

(2) RANGES: When setbacks vary by zone (e.g., 100-500 ft depending on zone), put the range string in 'value', set value_interpretation='range', AND populate range_low/range_high.

(3) TIERS: When a value depends on a band (capacity, distance, zone), emit ONE ROW PER TIER with value_interpretation='tiered' and the triggering band in 'condition'.

(4) DAY/NIGHT: When noise limits differ by time, create separate rows with condition='daytime' or 'nighttime' and specific_subject='daytime limit'/'nighttime limit'.

(5) FACILITY SCOPE vs TRIGGER: Put the governed facility type in 'applies_to' (e.g., 'Compressor station'); put the situational circumstance in 'condition' (e.g., 'nighttime'). Never mix the two.

(6) MIXED CLAUSES: When one clause includes both a measurable threshold and a separate non-numeric prohibition/exception, emit separate rows by semantic role (quantitative row for value/units/value_interpretation; qualitative row for non-numeric prohibition/exception).

(7) MONITORING PROTOCOL DECOMPOSITION: If one monitoring clause contains multiple measurable constraints (e.g., 'within 48 hours', 'for 72 hours', 'at 100 feet'), emit one quantitative row per measurable constraint using the matching rule_kind (deadline, duration, location).

(8) SITE-PLAN SUBMISSION DISTANCES: When a provision requires a site plan to 'show', 'list', or 'include' items within a certain distance (e.g., 'show structures within one mile of property lines'), this is a filing/reporting requirement — NOT a siting constraint. EXCLUDE these entirely. A developer cannot be blocked from siting by a paperwork radius; only extract distances that physically constrain WHERE a facility may be located.

(9) AMBIENT REFERENCE + ADDER PATTERN (for noise like 'ambient + 7 dB'):
   - Capture as: value=7 (the adder), ambient_reference_level='pre-development ambient level' (the reference)
   - Use value_category='quantitative', value_interpretation='maximum'
   - Example: 'shall not exceed ambient + 7 dB daytime' → value=7, units='dB', ambient_reference_level='pre-development ambient level', specific_subject='daytime adder', condition='daytime'
   - The adder IS the extractable numeric magnitude; the reference goes in ambient_reference_level

(10) PRIORITY FEATURES (extract if present and gas-specific):
   - property lines distance: setback from property boundaries (feet/meters)
   - distance between compressor stations: separation between gas compressor facilities (feet/meters)
   - roads distance: setback from street/right-of-way (feet/meters)
   - water bodies distance: setback from water features (feet/meters)
   - residential buildings distance: setback from homes (feet/meters)
   - schools/hospitals/community structures distance: setback from sensitive uses (feet/meters)
   - noise: ONLY the dBA/dB limit values (daytime/nighttime max levels). EXCLUDE: monitoring protocols, testing procedures, deadlines, durations, equipment standards
   - structures distance: setback from unnamed/generic structures (feet/meters). EXCLUDE definition clauses describing setback-zone contents.
   - front yard distance: front lot line setback for the facility (feet/meters)
   - minimum lot size: minimum parcel area (acres or square feet), value_interpretation='minimum'
   - zoning districts: qualitative + rule_kind='approval'; district codes in applicable_values, value_interpretation='enumerated'; one row per obligation level (allowed / conditional / prohibited)
   - fencing: height limits AND qualitative presence/opacity mandates (e.g., 'security fencing required', 'opaque fence shall enclose the facility'). EXCLUDE materials, gate hardware, landscaping
   - enclosure: required/prohibited mandates, quantitative or qualitative (e.g., 'all compressor units shall be housed in a fully enclosed building'). EXCLUDE architectural finish detail

(11) CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT (CUP) DEDUPLICATION:
   When a zoning ordinance lists 'Compressor Stations (Conditional Use Permit)' or similar in a use matrix/table AND a separate detailed ordinance section explicitly states 'A conditional use permit is required,' extract ONLY the 'permit_approval' row (the direct statement from the detailed section). Do NOT also extract a 'zoning_districts' summary row for the same obligation level and facility type. The detailed 'permit_approval' row is more authoritative and specific. Compilation will deduplicate any redundant rows by preferring permit_approval over zoning_districts when both state the same obligation.
   - permit_approval: any jurisdiction-level permit or approval gate (special permit, conditional use permit, site plan approval). Use rule_kind='approval', value_category='qualitative'.
     CRITICAL: Do NOT use 'enclosure' for permit/approval requirements.

feature.description: Standardized feature name (the WHAT axis). Use these exact values for cross-jurisdiction consistency. SCOPE: Only gas-specific or gas+facility constraints. EXCLUDE generic residential/commercial zoning. GAS-APPLICABILITY TEST (replaces topic-based exclusion): A yard setback, lot-size, or zoning-district rule IS extractable when it binds a natural gas facility — either stated directly ("a compressor station shall have a minimum front yard of 100 feet") or by a district table row naming gas/utility/energy uses. It is NOT extractable when it appears in a residential/commercial dimensional table with no gas linkage. Topic alone never disqualifies a rule; only absence of gas applicability does. 'structures distance': setback from buildings/structures generally, used ONLY when the ordinance does NOT name a specific occupancy type — e.g., "any occupied structure", "all buildings", "any inhabited dwelling or structure". PRECEDENCE: if the ordinance names a type (residential, school, hospital, civic), use the specific feature instead. Never emit both a specific-type row and a 'structures distance' row for the same clause. 'front yard distance': setback from the front/street-facing lot line for a gas facility structure. Use this instead of 'property lines distance' whenever the ordinance uses front-yard framing. 'minimum lot size': minimum parcel area required to site the facility (acres or square feet). Quantitative; value_interpretation='minimum'. 'zoning districts': which districts permit, conditionally permit, or prohibit the facility. Use value_category='qualitative', rule_kind='approval', and list district codes in applicable_values with value_interpretation='enumerated'. Emit SEPARATE rows per obligation level: obligation='allowed' for by-right districts, 'conditional' for conditional/special-use districts, 'prohibited' for banned districts. Do not merge districts with different obligation levels into one row. 'permit_approval': a jurisdiction-level gate requiring a permit, special permit, conditional use permit, or site plan approval before a natural gas facility may be sited or operated. Use this — NOT 'enclosure' — when the requirement is about obtaining authorization from a planning board, zoning board, or similar authority. EXCLUDE generic infrastructure permits (road access, driveway, utility connection) that apply to any construction project — only capture permits specific to siting the gas facility itself. Do NOT use 'enclosure' for permit/approval requirements.

rule_kind.description:
Canonical requirement shape for stronger cross-model alignment in validation. 'limit' for bounded thresholds, 'deadline' for due windows, 'duration' for sustained periods, 'location' for siting/setback placement constraints, 'equipment_standard' for required hardware/build standards, 'submission' for report/filing deliverables, 'approval' for permit/authorization gates, and 'monitoring' for qualitative testing/measurement protocols without fixed numeric magnitude. If a monitoring clause includes explicit numeric timing/distance thresholds, split into quantitative `deadline`/`duration`/`location` rows.

SITING-CRITICAL RESTRICTIONS BY FEATURE: For the 'noise' feature: only extract rule_kind='limit'. Monitoring, deadline, duration, submission, equipment_standard rule_kinds for noise are operational details — exclude them. For 'fencing': use rule_kind='limit' for height values and rule_kind='equipment_standard' for a required fence/opacity mandate; exclude equipment_standard rows for locking hardware, material composition, and landscaping. For 'enclosure': use rule_kind='equipment_standard' for a required or prohibited enclosure mandate, quantitative or qualitative; exclude architectural finish detail. For 'zoning districts' and 'minimum lot size': use rule_kind='approval' and rule_kind='limit' respectively.

specific_subject.description: Sub-aspect of the feature that distinguishes this record from other rows sharing the same feature (WHAT axis). Participates in the dedup key. Use the ordinance's own framing. Null when the feature is already specific enough. REQUIRED for 'property lines distance': set specific_subject to 'rear yard', 'side yard', or 'from property line' (general/unspecified). Never leave null on this feature — rear and side setbacks are frequently different values and must remain distinct rows.

applies_to.description: Facility type or scope the requirement governs (WHAT/WHERE axis), in the document's own terminology. Describes the kind of facility the rule binds. This is NOT the situational trigger (use 'condition') and NOT the obligation. Null when the requirement applies to all natural gas pipeline/compressor facilities generally. NOTE: 'Oil and gas operations' is acceptable ONLY when the ordinance's definition of 'oil and gas operations' explicitly includes natural gas compressor stations (e.g., PA statute 58 P.S. § 3201 et seq.). In such cases, the requirement is siting-critical and should be extracted with applies_to='Oil and gas operations'.

requirement_description.description: Clean, obligation-free description of the regulated action or object (WHAT axis). NEVER include obligation language — no 'required', 'shall', 'may', 'must', 'prohibited'. Used for qualitative requirements; null for purely quantitative rows. For qualitative requirements with relative-reference limits (e.g., 'must not exceed pre-development ambient noise levels'), state the reference standard here (e.g., 'Noise shall not exceed pre-development ambient levels within 300 feet') — do NOT leave this null while classifying the row as qualitative.
examples: Noise shall not exceed pre-development ambient levels within 300 feet
Located on a platted lot approved by the city and recorded in county records

value_category.description:
REQUIRED. How this requirement's value should be interpreted (HOW MUCH axis). 'quantitative' = a fixed, extractable numeric magnitude lives in 'value' (distance, dBA, acres, MW, hours, %, $). 'qualitative' = there is no fixed numeric magnitude; the substance lives in 'requirement_description' and 'value' must be null. Independent of 'obligation': a quantitative limit can be conditional and a qualitative item can be required.

CRITICAL: If the limit is a relative reference ('shall not exceed pre-development ambient levels', 'shall not exceed neighboring property baseline') or a procedural/approval requirement with no fixed numeric value, classify as 'qualitative' — the reference phrase belongs in 'requirement_description'. NEVER classify as 'quantitative' when 'value' would be null. If your 'reasoning' concludes 'no magnitude → qualitative', set value_category='qualitative'. Exception: formula-based procedural rules (where the value is determined by referencing another zoning variable with no extractable number) use value_category='qualitative' + value_interpretation='formula'.

value.description: For quantitative requirements, the numeric magnitude ONLY (e.g., 500, 55, 8). Use a range string (e.g., '100-500') when the provision states a span, set value_interpretation='range', and populate range_low/range_high. For qualitative requirements set value to null and describe the requirement in requirement_description. NEVER embed units or obligation words ('required', 'may', 'shall') in value.

value_interpretation.description: How the value is bounded or structured (HOW MUCH axis). 'exact' = single fixed value ('shall be 35 feet'); 'minimum' = floor ('at least', 'no less than'); 'maximum' = ceiling ('shall not exceed' a FIXED absolute level — not ambient-referenced). 'above_ambient' = value is an ADDER above an ambient baseline ('shall not exceed ambient + X dB') — use this instead of 'maximum' whenever the limit references a measured baseline; include the baseline description in notes if not already in source_verbatim. 'range' = a span — populate range_low and range_high; 'formula' = value is determined by a formula, lookup, or rule referencing another variable (e.g., 'setback equals the distance required by the adjoining zoning district' — use this, NOT 'tiered', when there is no extractable numeric value and the rule references an external lookup); when using formula set value=null and describe the rule in requirement_description; 'tiered' = value depends on a band — emit one row per tier; 'enumerated' = a discrete set — pair with applicable_values. Null for qualitative requirements.

units.description: Unit of measurement for a quantitative value. Null for qualitative requirements.

range_low.description: Lower bound of the span when 'value' is a range (e.g., 100 for '100-500'). Domain-agnostic: works for distances, dBA, MW, acres, etc. Null unless value_interpretation='range'.

range_high.description: Upper bound of the span when 'value' is a range (e.g., 500 for '100-500'). Domain-agnostic: works for distances, dBA, MW, acres, etc. Null unless value_interpretation='range'.

obligation.description:
REQUIRED. How binding the requirement is (HOW BINDING axis). Never place obligation language inside 'value' or 'requirement_description'.

Normalization rules:
- Quantitative limits/setbacks/windows should use obligation='required'; encode direction in value_interpretation (minimum/maximum/range) even when wording is negative (e.g., 'shall not exceed', 'shall not be within').
- Reserve obligation='prohibited' for qualitative bans with no measurable threshold.
- For permit-gated phrasing ('may be permitted only through ... permit'), encode the permit gate as obligation='required' on the approval row.

- 'required': mandatory — 'shall', 'must', 'is required', 'no less than'.
- 'prohibited': forbidden qualitative bans — 'shall not', 'no person shall', 'may not', 'is not permitted', 'prohibited'.
- 'conditional': discretionary authority — 'may require', 'at the discretion of', 'as a condition of approval', 'unless waived'.
- 'allowed': explicitly permitted with no mandate — 'is permitted', 'may be located', 'is allowed'.
- 'recommended': non-binding advisory — 'should', 'encouraged', 'best available technology'.
- 'informational': definitions, procedures, measured baselines, or referenced external standards with no direct obligation.

When multiple verbs appear, precedence: prohibited > required > conditional > recommended > allowed > informational. Cite the trigger language in 'reasoning'.

condition.description: Situational trigger or circumstance that governs WHEN or WHERE the requirement applies (WHEN/WHERE axis). Must be a SHORT phrase only — examples: 'nighttime', 'daytime only', 'capacity exceeds 3 MW', 'when in AG zone', 'after a signed complaint is received'. NEVER put the substance of the requirement here — if a sentence describes what is regulated rather than when/where it applies, it belongs in 'requirement_description' or 'source_verbatim'. Not the facility type (use 'applies_to'). Not the obligation. Null if the requirement applies unconditionally.
examples: after a signed complaint is received

applicable_values.description: Parallel interchangeable atomic values that share an IDENTICAL obligation, condition, and evidence. Use ONLY when (a) the values are categorical/enumerated (e.g., permitted district codes, acceptable permit types, equipment options) and (b) all share the same obligation + condition + source. Pair with value_interpretation='enumerated'. Null when a single value applies.

source_verbatim.description: Exact operative clause copied word-for-word from the ordinance (EVIDENCE axis). Never paraphrase — this is the audit anchor. If the passage exceeds 50 words, quote the operative head, insert '…', then the tail. Null only if no single passage can be quoted.
examples: ...shall not exceed a maximum of 55 dBa.
...may require the temporary or permanent erection...of sound barriers...

summary.description: Human-readable summary of the requirement (EVIDENCE axis). May be paraphrased for clarity. Use 'source_verbatim' for the exact quote. Include enough context for verification.

reasoning.description: Terse 'trigger → label' rationale (EVIDENCE axis), <=15 words, citing the governing verb and the value_category decision. Goes in ignore_fields and is hidden from compiled output. Null if self-evident.

section.description: Specific ordinance section/article reference (EVIDENCE axis, e.g., 'Sec. 12-5-106', 'Article 5 § 552', '§ 270-4.10').

notes.description: Additional context not captured elsewhere: measurement conditions, exceptions, cross-references.

anyOf.description: Formula rows (rule references external lookup with no extractable number) may use formula even with value_category=qualitative.
Enumerated rows (discrete categorical set in applicable_values, e.g. permitted zoning district codes) may use enumerated even with value_category=qualitative.
